video_title: How Concerned Should Warriors Be About Steph Curry? + Other Injury Concerns Around NBA

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Blazers' salary cap flexibility and contract management strategy
quotes.excerpt: The Blazers have a couple of the best contracts in the league.
quotes.quote: The Blazers have a couple of the best contracts in the league. When you think of Toumani Camara's contract, which I think he's in the first year of like a four and 80. It's not cheap, but for him, an elite three and D player, they did a great job and they won two games off the strength of that. Nobody can beat the Thunder. It was a two-game home stand, but they still had a good performance. I think Victor Wembanyama is the best contract in the league this year because he's still on his rookie deal. So that's got an asterisk, but Toumani Camara this year at 13.1 million and next year it dips to 11.8 million for the time being.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater

text_blocks.speaker: Anthony Slater
text_blocks.text: You want to know the problem with that contract though? It's so good you can't extend off of it. This was the Austin Reaves thing. There's several other examples in the past, but that's going to become kind of tense for the Blazers because you have to go into unrestricted free agency if you are them.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: No, you don't. This is a Bobby Marks thing. So, by the way, I want to also point out that Damian Lillard at the mid-level exception at 13 million for his output is also a very good contract.

quotes.excerpt: It's so good you can't extend off of it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry's oblique injury and recovery timeline
quotes.excerpt: Golden State's Stephen Curry has an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
quotes.quote: You were in Houston on Wednesday night when Steph went down in the first quarter, grabbing at his side, and then the Warriors announced on Thursday a torn oblique, re-evaluated in two weeks. The Warriors flying high, Steph averaging 30, they had won eight in a row, and that was a major come down and the Rockets broke their streak.

quotes.speaker: Anthony Slater
quotes.summary_phrase: Steph Curry's injury progression during the game
quotes.excerpt: He did it, tore the oblique, whatever, tweaked it, in two minutes into the game.
quotes.quote: He did it, tore the oblique, whatever, tweaked it, in two minutes into the game. You were watching him go through all of his movements and he's actually trying floaters and get knocked to the floor while between possessions he's grabbing at it. He actually came off a screen from Draymond Green up top, shot a three, made it. It was a nice play like over Amen Thompson and as he's doing his celebration, tap the stomach, point upstairs, he's screaming because he's feeling pain from shooting the three, and then asked out of the game.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeff Stotts' data on oblique strain recovery times
quotes.excerpt: The average time lost for nondescript oblique strains is 4.8 games (13 days).
quotes.quote: I was watching this Jeff Stotts tweet from InStreetClothes because he has the unprecedented database on this and he said, 'Like most strains, time lost for oblique strains is based on severity of the injury. The average time lost for nondescript oblique strains is 4.8 games (13 days), but that number jumps to 16 games (38 days) when moderate/severe strains are isolated.' So, again, based on that data, which is as good of a data as you're going to find on injuries in any league in the NBA, it would indicate, not for sure say, but it would indicate that it's not nondescript, that it's moderate.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst

quotes.quote: Karl-Anthony Towns 21 points, 13 and a half rebounds, which leads the NBA right now, 55% shooting overall, 40% from three. I mean, great.
